items.prompt:
Characters' spoken words in a story are called:
A) dialogue
B) summary
C) heading

Details that appeal to the senses are:
A) sensory language
B) counterclaims
C) citations

The speed at which a story unfolds is its:
A) pacing
B) title
C) margin

Which sentence SHOWS rather than tells?
A) 'His jaw tightened and he slammed the locker shut.'
B) 'He was angry.'
C) 'It was an angry moment.'
items.answer: A) 'His jaw tightened and he slammed the locker shut.'

solution.answer: A) 'His jaw tightened and he slammed the locker shut.'

items.prompt:
'Hours later' is an example of a:
A) time transition
B) claim
C) citation

steps: Signals a shift. Key is A.

items.prompt:
An 8th-grade narrative's conclusion should:
A) reflect on the meaning of the events
B) introduce a new topic
C) list sources
items.answer: A) reflect on the meaning of the events

solution.answer: A) reflect on the meaning of the events

items.prompt:
Why might a writer slow the PACING during a climactic scene?
A) to build suspense and emphasize the key moment
B) to end the story faster
C) to remove all detail
items.answer: A) to build suspense and emphasize the key moment

steps: Pacing controls tension. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) to build suspense and emphasize the key moment

items.prompt:
Which BEST uses dialogue to reveal character?
A) '"I don't lie, not even to win," she said, setting down the trophy.'
B) 'She said something.'
C) 'There was talking.'
items.answer: A) '"I don't lie, not even to win," she said, setting down the trophy.'

steps: Dialogue + action reveal character. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) '"I don't lie, not even to win," she said, setting down the trophy.'
